findings.description: The reports_archive bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so there is no enforced default encryption (KMS/CMK) for objects written to it.
The ledger_exports bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so ledger export objects are stored without an enforced encryption-at-rest configuration.
The model_artifacts bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so ML model artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
The ops_runbooks bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so runbook content is stored without enforced encryption at rest.

The audit_trail bucket sets acl = "log-delivery-write", granting the global LogDelivery group write and read-ACP on this bucket. Because this is also the tamper-evidence/log destination, that preconfigured ACL means any AWS account can be granted log-delivery write by making this bucket their log target, permitting log injection or overwriting in the audit store.

The uploaded object targets reports_archive, which has no default encryption, and the object itself specifies no server_side_encryption, so this vendor roster (potentially containing personal data) is stored unencrypted.
